previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with IgA multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, was admitted for worsening cellulitis around a chronic left leg ulcer after using a hot tub. He was afebrile and denied pain. Blood cultures were negative, but wound cultures grew group B strep, Bacteroides fragilis, and coagulase-negative staph. He was treated with IV antibiotics, initially cefepime then switched to piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn) for a 14-day course to be completed at home via a newly placed PICC line. MRI and X-ray ruled out osteomyelitis. His chemotherapy was held during admission and successfully resumed prior to discharge. He also received IV furosemide for acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, with improvement in edema, and was restarted on oral lasix. His hemolytic anemia remained stable on prednisone, and diabetes was managed with insulin. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for follow-up in oncology, infectious disease, and primary care.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  Non-invasive Doppler evaluation of the arterial inflow to both
lower extremities.

HISTORY:  ___ male with chronic left shin and right toe wounds. 
Request is to evaluate for arterial inflow disease.

TECHNIQUE:  Segmental blood pressure measurements, Doppler waveform analysis
and pulse volume recordings were attempted.

FINDINGS:  This a markedly limited study as the patient's lower extremity
vessels are non-compressible.  This yields falsely elevated pressures and
non-reliable ankle-brachial indices.  Doppler waveform analysis does
demonstrate triphasic waveforms throughout both right and left lower
extremities, however, with satisfactory amplitude pulse volume recordings.

IMPRESSION:  Non-compressible vessels and therefore non-recordable
ankle-brachial indices.  Doppler evaluation, however, demonstrates triphasic
waveforms throughout both right and left lower extremities with satisfactory
amplitude on pulse volume recording, however, again this is limited due to
vessel non-compressibility.

EXAMINATION:  MR FOOT ___ CONTRAST RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with history of recurrent cellulitis and left
second toe infection  // assess for osteomyelitis       It should be noted
that the order requisition for the exam states that the patient has a history
of a left second toe infection, however previous documentation in the ___
medical record states that the patient is a history of right second toe
infection.

TECHNIQUE:  Imaging performed at 1.5 using the QuadFoot coil. Sequences of the
right forefoot include axial, coronal and sagittal T1, sagittal and coronal
STIR, coronal T1 fat saturated, and postcontrast axial sagittal and coronal T1
fat saturated images after the uneventful administration of 10 mL of Gadavist.
Subtracted images were subsequently obtained..

COMPARISON:  Radiographs of the right foot ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is a soft tissue defect overlying the head of the second distal phalanx
compatible with the patient's known ulcer with a linear tract of fluid
extending to the head of the second distal phalanx. There is marrow signal
abnormality within the the head of the second distal phalanx with T1
hypointensity, STIR hyperintensity and enhancement on post-contrast imaging
consistent with osteomyelitis. No signal to drainable, enhancing fluid
collection is seen.  There is surrounding soft tissue swelling.

There are foci of T1 hypointensity, STIR hyperintensity which demonstrate
enhancement compatible with erosive changes at the lateral aspect of the first
metatarsophalangeal joint as well as at the tarsometatarsal joints diffusely.

There is diffuse nonspecific subcutaneous soft tissue edema along the dorsum
of the foot which may reflect cellulitis.

The flexor and extensor tendons are normal in appearance.

IMPRESSION: 

Soft tissue ulceration over the second distal phalanx with a linear tract of
fluid extending to the head of the distal phalanx where there are signal
changes compatible with osteomyelitis.

Erosive changes at the lateral aspect of the first metatarsophalangeal joint
as well as at the tarsometatarsal joints diffusely. While erosion can be seen
in the setting of infection, multifocality in this case suggests a systemic
process such as rheumatoid arthritis, gout or psoriatic arthritis. Although an
unusual manifestation, the differential diagnosis could include lyme disease.
Clinical correlation is requested.

Diffuse nonspecific soft tissue edema over the dorsum of the foot which may
represent cellulitis.

FINDINGS: 

There is no fracture or dislocation.  A subtle lucent area of the left distal
femur may correspond to a multiple myeloma lesion. Thickening of the soleal
line is noted. There is no area of cortical destruction or lucency in the
tibia concerning for osteomyelitis.  Moderate degenerative changes are present
in the medial and patellofemoral compartments of the knee. Calcaneal spurs are
noted. Mild pretibial soft tissue thickening is noted.

IMPRESSION: 

1. No findings concerning for osteomyelitis in the tibia.
2.  Lucent area of the at left distal femur, which may represent a multiple
myelomatous deposit.
